newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Simsmetal scraps plan to buy Wanless.
newsitem.headline: Simsmetal scraps plan to buy Wanless.

text.p: Metal recycler Simsmetal Ltd said on Thursday that it would not proceed with its attempt to acquire Wanless Metal Industries Pty Ltd due to opposition from the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC).

"Whilst disappointed with both the ACCC's conclusion and reasons given for that conclusion, in particular the ACCC's narrow interpretation of the relevant Australian markets, Simsmetal had decided, based on legal advice and its desire to devote its full resources to the pursuit of other opportunities, especially in the international arena, not to pursue this matter further," the company said.
Simsmetal did not say how much it planned to pay for Wanless, which has 80 employees and eight sites in the state of Queensland to receive ferrous and non-ferrous products.
Metalcorp Ltd, the nation's second largest recycler behind Simsmetal, said on March 25 that it wanted to buy Wanless but noted that Simsmetal had first right of refusal.
The ACCC, the anti-monopolies regulator, told Wanless on May 28 that the Simsmetal offer would reduce competition in Queensland and that the bid would be blocked.
